---
title: "2. Systems Thinking"
---

## Overview

This module introduces systems thinking as a framework for understanding the complex and interconnected nature of health systems and malaria transmission dynamics. Participants explore how interventions, behaviours, environmental factors, and health system components interact, and how these interactions influence programme outcomes and decision-making.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="default"}
## Learning Objectives

By the end of this module, participants should be able to:

-   Understand what systems thinking is, and how it applies to malaria programmes

-   Identify how interactions within complex systems influence disease outcomes

-   Explain how systems thinking can improve modelling and decision-making for malaria
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="default"}
## Key Concepts

-   Complex adaptive systems

-   Causal loop diagrams

-   Interconnections and feedback loops

-   Non-linear effects and unintended consequences

-   Systems mapping

-   Multi-sectoral influences on malaria outcomes
:::

### Practical Exercise

**Exercise Title:** Mapping the Malaria System

**Instructions:\
**In groups, participants develop a causal loop diagram showing factors influencing malaria burden in a selected setting. Groups are comprised of 3-5 fellows, each allocated to focus on one of the following system elements:

-   Access to care

-   Data surveillance systems

-   Drug resistance and availability of drugs

-   Acceptance of interventions

-   Climate change and environmental factors

-   Funding availability

The exercise can be done using software or analog with poster paper, markers, and sticky notes.

Groups present their causal loop diagrams and identify how the different system elements intersect and interact across the groups. During the faciliated discussion, there is an opportunity to consider where modelling could support decision-making within the system.

### Facilitator Guidance

-   Draw connections between programme operations, funding, behaviour, and outcomes

-   Support participants in visualising relationships and dependencies

-   Reinforce that systems thinking helps frame better modelling questions

## Materials and Resources

-   Introductory slide deck

-   Example causal loop diagrams

-   Flipcharts or digital collaboration tools
